extracted.intended_audience: Users of GAP (mathematicians and computational algebraists) working with Lie algebras, modules, magma rings, and polynomial/rational-function constructions
extracted.subtask_description: Reference-manual guidance for using GAP functions that construct and manipulate Lie-algebra modules and cohomology, admissible lattices, magma rings, and polynomial indeterminates. Covers representations, required argument formats, return formats, and implementation/printing conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of s-cochains
rubrics_metrics.description: An s-cochain of a module V over a Lie algebra L is represented as a list of r lists (r = dim V). Each of the r lists contains entries of the form [[i1, i2, ..., is], lambda], where 1 ≤ i1 < ... < is ≤ dim L, and lambda is the non-zero coefficient in that basis component. Only entries with non-zero coefficients are stored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This representation implies every s-tuple (i1,...,is) can give rise to r basis elements. Example provided: a 2-cochain for a 4-dimensional V is shown as [ [ [[1,2],2] ], [ ], [ [[1,2],1/2] ], [ ] ].

rubrics_metrics.name: 0-cochain representation
rubrics_metrics.description: By definition, 0-cochains are constant maps c(x)=v_c for all x in L and are represented simply by the list [v_c].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 0-cochains use a distinct representation from s>0 cochains; ExtRepOfObj returns that representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cochain construction (Cochain function)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cochain(V, s, obj) constructs an s-cochain given the data in obj with respect to the Lie-algebra module V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If s is non-zero then obj must be a list. The result is an object of the cochain category; ExtRepOfObj(c) returns the list representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: CochainSpace
rubrics_metrics.description: CochainSpace(V, s) returns the vector space of all s-cochains with respect to the module V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: for a 3-dimensional adjoint module and s=2, CochainSpace returns <vector space of dimension 9 over Rationals> and BasisVectors list of <2-cochain> elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: ValueCochain usage
rubrics_metrics.description: ValueCochain(c, y1, y2, ..., ys) returns the value of the s-cochain c applied to the s elements y1,...,ys in the Lie algebra. Alternatively call ValueCochain(c, [y1,...,ys]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows ValueCochain(c, Basis(L)[2], Basis(L)[1]) returning a vector in V (like (-1)*v.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: LieCoboundaryOperator
rubrics_metrics.description: LieCoboundaryOperator(c) takes an s-cochain c and returns the (s+1)-cochain obtained by applying the Lie coboundary operator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated application increases cochain degree (example: c -> c1 (<3-cochain>) -> c2 (<4-cochain>)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cocycles operation
rubrics_metrics.description: Cocycles(V, s) returns the space of all s-cocycles for module V; i.e., the kernel of the coboundary operator restricted to s-cochains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Cocycles(V,2) returning <vector space of dimension 7 over Rationals>.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coboundaries operation
rubrics_metrics.description: Coboundaries(V, s) returns the space of all s-coboundaries for module V; i.e., the image of the coboundary operator applied to s-1-cochains. By definition the space of all 0-coboundaries is zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Coboundaries(V,2) returned a vector space with 9 generators; Dimension(last) maybe used to compute cohomology dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsCochain categories
rubrics_metrics.description: IsCochain(obj) and IsCochainCollection(obj) designate the category membership for cochain objects and collections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to dispatch appropriate methods on cochain objects in GAP's category system.

rubrics_metrics.name: DominantWeights
rubrics_metrics.description: DominantWeights(R, maxw) returns a list of two lists: the first contains the dominant weights (written on the basis of fundamental weights) of the irreducible highest-weight module with highest weight maxw over the Lie algebra with root system R; the second contains the corresponding levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Level of a weight μ defined as μ = λ − Σ_i k_i α_i (λ highest weight), level = Σ_i k_i. Example output given for F4.

rubrics_metrics.name: DominantCharacter
rubrics_metrics.description: DominantCharacter(L, maxw) or DominantCharacter(R, maxw) returns two lists: the dominant weights of the highest-weight module with highest weight maxw and the multiplicities of those weights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First argument may be a semisimple Lie algebra or a root system; output format mirrors DominantWeights but includes multiplicities.

rubrics_metrics.name: DecomposeTensorProduct
rubrics_metrics.description: DecomposeTensorProduct(L, w1, w2) returns a decomposition of V1 ⊗ V2 (highest-weight modules with highest weights w1 and w2) as a direct sum of irreducible highest-weight modules: two lists, one of highest weights (sorted) and one of multiplicities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithm uses Klimyk’s formula; examples show returned multiplicities and weights.

rubrics_metrics.name: DimensionOfHighestWeightModule
rubrics_metrics.description: DimensionOfHighestWeightModule(L, w) returns the dimension of the highest-weight module over semisimple Lie algebra L with dominant weight w.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The algorithm uses Weyl’s dimension formula; example returns very large integer for a 4-component weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissible lattice (Kostant theorem) for UEA
rubrics_metrics.description: For semisimple L (char 0) with Chevalley basis, the elements x(n)_α = x_α^n / n! and y(n)_α = y_α^n / n! generate a subring of U(L) that is a lattice (free Z-module) and invariant under the x(n)_α; such a lattice is called an admissible lattice in U(L).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference to Kostant and PBW theorem; this justifies constructing generators and representing lattice elements as in subsequent functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: LatticeGeneratorsInUEA
rubrics_metrics.description: LatticeGeneratorsInUEA(L) (L semisimple, char 0) returns a list of generators of an admissible lattice in U(L) relative to the Chevalley basis: first negative root vectors y1..ys, then positive root vectors x1..xs, and finally the Cartan elements printed as (hi/k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Printed form (hi/k) means hi/k etc.; yi^(m) is printed as yi^(m) meaning entering yi^m yields m!*yi^(m) in output. Product ordering is specified: y(mi) in order of positive roots, then (hi/ki), then x(ni).

rubrics_metrics.name: ObjByExtRep for UEALatticeElement
rubrics_metrics.description: ObjByExtRep(F, descr) creates a UEALattice element. A UEALattice element is represented by a list [m1, c1, m2, c2, ...] where ci are coefficients and mi are monomials; a monomial is a list [ind1, e1, ind2, e2, ...].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indices 1..N correspond to negative root vectors, N+1..2N to positive root vectors, 2N+1..2N+rank to Cartan elements printed as (h_i/e_i). Zero element is [], identity is [[],1]. Example shows ExtRepOfObj output format.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsWeightRepElement representation
rubrics_metrics.description: IsWeightRepElement objects represent vectors used to construct elements of highest-weight modules. A WeightRepElement is a list [v1,c1,v2,c2,...] where vi are basis (weight) vectors; a basis vector is [k, mon, wt] where k is index, mon an UEALatticeElement, wt the weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A WeightRepElement is printed as mon*v0 (v0 highest weight vector). ExtRepOfObj returns the list; ObjByExtRep(list,fam) reconstructs the object.

rubrics_metrics.name: HighestWeightModule behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: HighestWeightModule(L, wt) returns the highest weight module with highest weight wt for semisimple Lie algebra L (char 0). Elements of this module lie in category IsLeftAlgebraModuleElement; ExtRepOfObj(v) for v in the module returns a WeightRepElement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example constructs a 224-dimensional module over a direct sum Lie algebra and inspects basis vectors and ExtRepOfObj outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: TensorProductOfAlgebraModules
rubrics_metrics.description: TensorProductOfAlgebraModules(list) or TensorProductOfAlgebraModules(V, W) returns the tensor product of algebra modules as an algebra module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inputs must be algebra modules (modules over an algebra/Lie algebra). Example shows constructing triple tensor product with resulting dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: ExteriorPowerOfAlgebraModule
rubrics_metrics.description: ExteriorPowerOfAlgebraModule(V, k) returns the k-th exterior power of algebra module V, as an algebra module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: V must be an algebra module over a Lie algebra; example shows ExteriorPowerOfAlgebraModule(V,3) with printed basis elements and module actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: SymmetricPowerOfAlgebraModule
rubrics_metrics.description: SymmetricPowerOfAlgebraModule(V, k) returns the k-th symmetric power of algebra module V, as an algebra module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: V must be an algebra module; example shows symmetric action and printed outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: FreeMagmaRing (definition & common examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: FreeMagmaRing(R, M) constructs the free magma ring RM over ring-with-one R on magma M. Typical examples include polynomial rings, group rings, Laurent polynomial rings, free associative algebras, and free algebras.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: polynomial rings in GAP are not formally constructed as free magma rings; free Lie algebras are not magma rings because of Jacobi identity. The coefficient ring R and magma M are not subsets of RM; embeddings must be used explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: GroupRing
rubrics_metrics.description: GroupRing(R, G) constructs the group ring RG of group G over ring R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group rings are special cases of magma rings where the underlying magma is a group.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsFreeMagmaRing category and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: An object lies in IsFreeMagmaRing if it was constructed as a free magma ring; then attributes LeftActingDomain and UnderlyingMagma apply and yield the ring R and magma M such that D is RM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A magma ring may be generated by different magma representations abstractly; examples include group rings having alternative generating magmas.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsFreeMagmaRingWithOne synonym
rubrics_metrics.description: IsFreeMagmaRingWithOne is a synonym for the meet of IsFreeMagmaRing and IsMagmaWithOne.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category convenience for magma rings with identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsGroupRing category
rubrics_metrics.description: IsGroupRing(obj) indicates the magma ring is a group ring (underlying magma is a group).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for dispatch and properties specific to group rings.

rubrics_metrics.name: UnderlyingMagma attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: UnderlyingMagma(RM) returns/stores the underlying magma M of a free magma ring RM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to retrieve the generating magma; necessary because M is not implicitly a subset of RM.

rubrics_metrics.name: AugmentationIdeal attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: AugmentationIdeal(RG) returns the augmentation ideal of the group ring RG, i.e., the kernel of the trivial representation of RG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provided as an attribute/operation on group rings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default representation of magma ring elements
rubrics_metrics.description: IsMagmaRingObjDefaultRep: the default external representation of a magma ring element is a list of length 2: first position the zero coefficient, second a list containing coefficients at even positions and magma elements at odd positions, with ordering compatible with magma element ordering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is assumed arithmetic operations produce only normalized elements. Specific external representations exist for some rings (polynomials, free associative algebras).

rubrics_metrics.name: CoefficientsAndMagmaElements attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: CoefficientsAndMagmaElements(elm) returns a list that contains at odd positions the magma elements and at even positions their coefficients in elm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows treating magma-ring elements uniformly without relying on external representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: ZeroCoefficient attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: ZeroCoefficient(elm) returns the zero element of the coefficient ring R for an element elm of a magma ring RM (modulo relations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful when constructing elements via ElementOfMagmaRing.

rubrics_metrics.name: ElementOfMagmaRing operation
rubrics_metrics.description: ElementOfMagmaRing(Fam, zerocoeff, coeffs, mgmelms) constructs the element Σ_i coeffs[i] * m'_i where m'_i are images of mgmelms[i] embedded into the magma ring family Fam; zerocoeff must be the zero of the coefficient ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Efficient way to construct magma ring elements without creating many intermediate embedded magma elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories: IsElementOfFreeMagmaRing and family variants
rubrics_metrics.description: IsElementOfFreeMagmaRing(obj) and IsElementOfFreeMagmaRingCollection(obj) designate elements and collections of elements of a free magma ring; family variants indicate trivial normalization and efficient comparison methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these categories for method dispatch and family-specific optimizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for explicit embeddings (Embedding behavior)
rubrics_metrics.description: The coefficient ring R and magma M are not regarded as subsets of RM; one must use Embedding to map magma elements and ring elements into RM. Each call to FreeMagmaRing creates a new family, so identical-looking elements from different families are distinct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show embedding usage and pitfalls: elements from different group rings/families are not considered equal even if algebraically identical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magma rings modulo relations & normalization
rubrics_metrics.description: MagmaRingModuloRelations allows constructing magma rings with relations (e.g., free Lie algebras) but is limited to cases where a cheap normal form is known. NormalizedElementOfMagmaRingModuloRelations(F, descr) returns a normalized description so CoefficientsAndMagmaElements is well-defined and equal for equal elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IsMagmaRingModuloRelations indicates rings where each element has a unique normal form; such category not inherited to general factor structures (use finitely presented algebras mechanisms).

rubrics_metrics.name: MagmaRingModuloSpanOfZero
rubrics_metrics.description: MagmaRingModuloSpanOfZero(R, M, z) returns the magma ring R M modulo the relation identifying a magma element z with zero, provided z*m = z for all m in M (a 'zero element' in magma sense).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This constructs an example of a magma ring modulo relations; use when such a zero-like magma element exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical implementation details for magma rings
rubrics_metrics.description: Family behavior: each FreeMagmaRing creates a new family containing elements with coefficients in the family of R and magma elements in family of M, so arithmetic with coefficients outside R or magma elements outside M may create elements outside RM. No generic external representation exists for arbitrary free magma rings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polynomials and some algebras have specialized external representations; the default rep stores zero coefficient and a list with magma-element external reps and coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polynomials and rational functions: definitions & embeddings
rubrics_metrics.description: A polynomial ring over R is a free associative algebra over R; indeterminates are the free generators. If R is an integral domain, polynomial ring over R is an integral domain and has quotient field (rational functions) provided R is a UFD to avoid leading-coefficient issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GAP implements rational functions and will embed polynomials into rational functions implicitly; be aware of ring vs coefficient-object distinctions (zeros differ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indeterminate naming and numbering conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Indeterminates are internally represented by positive integers; by default printed as x_nr. Names (strings) can be assigned for nicer printing, but name strings do not necessarily correspond to variable/slot names in GAP variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When requesting indeterminates with certain names GAP picks the first not-yet-named indeterminates; IndeterminateNumberOfLaurentPolynomial(indet) returns the internal number; creating a named indeterminate when name exists returns the existing indeterminate unless :new option used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indeterminate function usage (Indeterminate / X)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indeterminate(R[, nr]) or Indeterminate(R[, name][, avoid]) or X synonyms return an indeterminate on ring R. If nr omitted defaults to 1. If avoid list is given, returns an indeterminate different from those in avoid. Setting name returns named indeterminate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: X is synonym for Indeterminate. Use avoid to get a fresh indeterminate distinct from a given list.

rubrics_metrics.name: IndeterminateNumberOfUnivariateRationalFunction behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: IndeterminateNumberOfUnivariateRationalFunction(rfun) returns the number of the indeterminate in which the univariate rational function rfun is expressed. A constant rational function might not possess an indeterminate number; in that case it defaults to 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two univariate polynomials may be considered in the same univariate polynomial ring if their indeterminate numbers match or one is constant; see CIUnivPols and related attributes.

rubrics_metrics.name: IndeterminateOfUnivariateRationalFunction
rubrics_metrics.description: IndeterminateOfUnivariateRationalFunction(rfun) returns the indeterminate object in which the univariate rational function rfun is expressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides direct access to the indeterminate object (cf. IndeterminateNumberOfUnivariateRationalFunction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indeterminate naming functions (Set/Has/Return)
rubrics_metrics.description: SetIndeterminateName(fam, nr, name) assigns name to indeterminate nr in family fam and errors if already named. IndeterminateName(fam,nr) returns the name or fail. HasIndeterminateName(fam,nr) tests whether a name is assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SetName method is provided to assign names to indeterminates. Example demonstrates naming and usage in printing and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: CIUnivPols (compatibility check for univariate polynomials)
rubrics_metrics.description: CIUnivPols(upol1, upol2) (mentioned) is a utility related to compatibility of univariate polynomials possibly in different rings/families (exact description not in this chunk).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced here as part of indeterminate handling and univariate polynomial family behaviors; see full documentation for CIUnivPols usage.
